results.title: DigitalOcean raises H100 rental prices 30% • The Weighted Average
results.author: Stephen Van Tran
highlights:
# DigitalOcean raises H100 rental prices 30%

08/02/26, 09:24 AM

DigitalOcean raised on-demand H100 GPU Droplet pricing 30%, from $3.39 to $4.41 per GPU-hour, while H200 pricing climbed from $3.44 to $4.47 on August 1. The provider’s pricing notice attributes the increases to strong demand, and its live GPU rate card lists the new prices; an eight-H100 workload running continuously now costs about $71,500 more per year. Operators should file the move beside China’s 34% AI-cloud price hike: capacity competition can overwhelm nominal model-efficiency gains, so infrastructure quotes need expiry dates in production budgets.

results.title: DigitalOcean GPU Droplets: What They Cost and What They Lose
results.author: Ansh Saxena
highlights:
> TL;DR: GPU Droplets are billed per second and priced per GPU: $4.41/hr for an H100, $4.47 for an H200, $2.59 for an MI300X, $1.57 for an L40S or RTX 6000 Ada, $0.76 for an RTX 4000 Ada, as of DigitalOcean's August 1, 2026 pricing. Against 1,044 live offers from nine providers, that is roughly double the market low on the small cards and about a third above the H100 median, but it is genuinely competitive on H200, where the market median is $4.59. The thing to actually plan around is storage: the 5 TiB "scratch" disk attached to every multi-GPU config is documented as non-persistent, is excluded from snapshots, and is lost when the Droplet is destroyed, and destroying is the only way to stop the meter, because a powered-off GPU Droplet keeps billing in full.

## What a GPU Droplet is

A GPU Droplet is an ordinary DigitalOcean Droplet with a GPU attached, in seven shapes. Every configuration below is from DigitalOcean's own GPU Droplet pricing page, which states its rates are "effective as of August 1, 2026":

| GPU | VRAM | Count | vCPU | RAM | Boot disk | Scratch disk | Per GPU/hr |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA HGX H200 | 141 GB | 1 or 8 | 24 | 240 GiB | 720 GiB NVMe | 5 TiB NVMe | $4.47 |
| NVIDIA HGX H100 | 80 GB | 1 or 8 | 20 | 240 GiB | 720 GiB NVMe | 5 TiB NVMe | $4.41 |
| AMD Instinct MI325X | 256 GB | 1 or 8 | 20 | 164 GiB | 720 GiB NVMe | 5 TiB NVMe | $3.80 |
| AMD Instinct MI300X | 192 GB | 1 or 8 | 20 | 240 GiB | 720 GiB NVMe | 5 TiB NVMe | $2.59 |
| NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada | 48 GB | 1 | 8 | 64 GiB | 500 GiB NVMe | N/A | $1.57 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 48 GB | 1 | 8 | 64 GiB | 500 GiB NVMe | N/A | $1.57 |
| NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada | 20 GB | 1 | 8 | 32 GiB | 500 GiB NVMe | N/A | $0.76 |

Two details worth pulling out of that table before the price comparison. The multi-GPU shapes are sold as 1 or 8. There is no 2, 4, or 6. And DigitalOcean's own two sources disagree on the billing floor: the pricing page says GPU Droplets are "billed per second with a 5-minute minimum billing period", while the Droplet pricing documentation says they are "billed per second with a minimum charge of 60 seconds or $0.01, whichever is higher". Both are DigitalOcean's; we have not been able to reconcile them, and on a workload of short bursty runs the difference is real, so budget for the five-minute floor.

On H100 it is above the median but not absurd: $4.41 against a $3.29 median across 81 offers. You are paying about a third over the middle of the market for the integration.

Worth keeping in mind on all of the above: this is a snapshot, not a floor. H100-class pricing has actually been climbing market-wide since mid-2025 after two years of decline, for reasons that have nothing to do with any single vendor. results.title: H100 Rental Prices to Rise by 40% After October 2025 | WEEX Crypto News
highlights:
By: www.tokenpost.kr|

08/04/2026 18:30:49

The one-year rental contract price for NVIDIA's H100 has increased by approximately 40%, rising from $1.70 in October 2025 to $2.35 in March 2026. As the use of AI expands from training to inference, supply bottlenecks and price disparities in the GPU rental market are widening. DigitalOcean announced that it will adjust the on-demand pricing and 12-month reservation prices for some GPU droplets starting August 1. According to the Silicon Data Index on August 3, the rental price for the H100 was reported at $2.78 on NeoCloud and $7.18 on hyperscalers. With the increasing demand for AI models, it is analyzed that a single user may require 10 to 100 times more compute from the latest tools. The impact of rising GPU rental prices on distributed compute token prices or mining profitability may vary depending on contract duration, region, and availability. According to analysis by Jera, the price range for the H100 has widened up to 18 times, and the GPU rental market remains fragmented.

results.title: Why Spiky Inference Traffic Breaks the Dedicated GPU Math
results.author: DigitalOcean Community
highlights:
A DigitalOcean H200 GPU Droplet needs to sustain 1,910 billable tokens per second, averaged over the billing period, to cost less per token than DO Serverless Inference. That figure is 46.9% of the measured 4,071.6 tok/s total-token throughput ceiling, calculated at the GPU Droplet rate of $4.47 per hour effective August 1, 2026, against serverless pricing of $0.65 per 1 million tokens. Engineers sizing GPU inference capacity track pricing shifts like this one on daily.dev before committing budget.

How did DigitalOcean's August 2026 GPU pricing change affect the dedicated versus serverless inference crossover point?

DigitalOcean raised its H200 GPU Droplet on-demand rate to $4.47 per GPU-hour effective August 1, 2026, matching the existing Dedicated Inference rate. Before that change, the GPU Droplet ran at $3.44/hour with a lower 36.1% utilization threshold, while Dedicated Inference carried a separate, higher floor for its managed-serving premium; now both products share one $4.47/hr rate and one 46.9% crossover. Teams comparing GPU Droplet and managed inference pricing can follow rate changes like this via daily.dev.

Correction (October 2026): An earlier version of this post said DigitalOcean raised Droplet prices 8–10% in June 2026. Our pricing history does not support that: the tracked s-1vcpu-1gb and s-2vcpu-4gb Droplets were unchanged from November 2025 through September 2026, and c-4 moved from $83 to $84 a month (about 1.2%). DigitalOcean's 2026 increase applied to select GPU Droplets, which we don't track. See Pricing History for the full record.

...

### DigitalOcean — an apparent compute spike was a billing-basis error

A later source audit found that the reported June increases came from multiplying DigitalOcean's API price_hourly by 730, rather than using its published monthly price. The hourly field uses a different billing-hour basis, so those values did not establish price changes. The published monthly prices are $6/mo for s-1vcpu-1gb, $24/mo for s-2vcpu-4gb, and $84/mo for c-4; checks now compare each monthly price divided by 730. The managed database Basic reference plans are listed at $15.15/mo and $60.90/mo. Missing or unmatched catalog plans are not assigned substitute prices.

...

If you run DigitalOcean Droplets, DigitalOcean's tracked Droplet prices were essentially flat (c-4 rose about 1.2%). The tracked s-1vcpu-1gb and s-2vcpu-4gb prices did not change from November 2025 through September 2026.
